newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-RAIN SOFTENS AUGUSTA NATIONAL FOR MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RAIN SOFTENS AUGUSTA NATIONAL FOR MASTERS.

text.p: A soft overnight rain that continued into Saturday morning softened Augusta National golf course for the third round of the Masters, but the benign playing conditions might not help the other 45 players overtake the Tiger Woods juggernaut.

Woods, the 21-year-old sensation, held a three-stroke lead over Colin Montgomerie of Britain going into the third round of the Masters after he shot a six-under-par 66 on Friday for the tournament's lowest round so far.

The three-time U.S. Amateur champion, who had a 36-hole total of eight-under-par 136, became the youngest player to lead any round of the Masters, supplanting Seve Ballesteros of Spain, who had held that distinction since the first round of the 1980 Masters.

While the rain softened Augusta National's notorious superfast greens, making them more receptive to approach shots, the moisture would also prevent tee shots from rolling very far, making the par-72 course play longer than its listed 6,925 yards.

That might be a problem for many players, but not for Woods -- who on both days hit a driver and a wedge to the green on the 500-yard 15th hole, which he eagled on Thursday. He missed an eight-foot eagle putt there on Friday.

Woods, who won standing ovations from Augusta's huge galleries with his awesome length and pinpoint iron play, was three shots clear of Montgomerie, the best player in Europe for the past four years, and another stroke ahead of Costantino Rocca of Italy, Montgomerie's Ryder Cup teammate.
Just below them on the leaderboard were seven players who have won at least one major championship, led by Jose Maria Olazabal of Spain, the 1994 Masters champion, and Fred Couples, the 1992 winner.
They were at three under par with Jeff Sluman, who won the 1988 PGA Championship and this year's Tucson Open.

Behind them at two under par were Nick Price of Zimbabwe, winner of the British Open and two PGA Championships, Paul Azinger, the 1993 PGA champion, and Paul Stankowski, who had led the first round until John Huston eagled the last hole to overtake him.

Also within striking distance at one under were veteran Tom Watson, winner of the 1981 Masters, 1982 U.S. Open and five British Opens, Ernie Els of South Africa, the 1994 U.S.Open champion, and Davis Love, who was runnerup in the 1995 Masters.
Still, the supremely confident Woods was the player to beat.
"I came here to win," he has said repeatedly.
